newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse October turnover 13 pct up m/m.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse October turnover 13 pct up m/m.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange on Thursday reported a 13 percent rise in its turnover during October, and traders attributed the rise to banks seeking fresh borrowing.
"Total turnover in October rose to 56.3 million dinars ($11.18 million) in 178 transactions, up on 49.6 million dinars in 148 deals in September," Dejan Vasovic of the Montenegro bourse told Reuters.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) decision to launch the reserve requirement in September squeezed liquidity out of the banking sector, Vasovic said.
This increased banks' thirst for money and they turned to the unofficial giro money market and increased the offer of their treasury bills, he added.
Monday's NBY decision to increase the reserve requirement to 15 from 10 percent, effective from November 11, would cause some liquidity problems among banks and temporarily weigh on market activity.
But later it will again translate into rising demand for new borrowing, Vasovic said.

Short-term securities accounted for 51.67 percent of the total turnover in October, while the giro money market segment, where banks trade their surplus liquidity, generated 48.33 percent of the monthly total, the bourse said.
The bourse reported no trade in the central bank short-term bonds because the NBY held no auction in October, Vasovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
